html:
The forced removal of tens of thousands of Israelites from the northern Kingdom of Israel by Assyria in the late 700s BCE. Its capital Samaria fell in 722 or 720 BCE, and the kingdom ended.

Deporting conquered peoples was standard Assyrian policy: it broke up resistance and moved labour where the empire needed it. Tiglath-Pileser III had already taken people from Galilee in 732 BCE. After the siege of Samaria under Shalmaneser V, Sargon II claimed to have carried off 27,290 people. The Bible says they were settled in upper Mesopotamia and the cities of the Medes, while other peoples were brought into Samaria.

The exiles were absorbed and vanished from history, which gave rise to the legend of the Ten Lost Tribes. The newcomers mixing with the Israelites who stayed are the traditional origin of the Samaritans. The southern kingdom of Judah survived until Babylon destroyed Jerusalem in 586 BCE.
sum: The forced removal of tens of thousands of Israelites from the northern Kingdom of Israel by Assyria in the late 700s BCE. Its capital Samaria fell in 722 or 720 BCE, and the kingdom ended.
